newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. renews peacekeeping mission in Macedonia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. renews peacekeeping mission in Macedonia.

text.p: With Albania still in turmoil, the U.N. Security Council on Wednesday agreed to extend for six months the 1,050 U.N. force in neighbouring Macedonia, a former Yugoslav republic.
Russia, which wanted the mission that includes 500 Americans, closed or sharply reduced, agreed to the extension because of the Albanian situation.

But Ambassador Sergei Lavrov told the council the mission should be restructured and "concentrated in the Albanian area." He said a there should be a "speedy reduction" in the force as soon as circumstances allow.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, in a report earlier this month, said the unsettled situation in Albania ruled out ending or reducing the mission now. But he said it might be possible to begin a reduction of 300 troops after four months, depending on the situation at the time.

The council, in its resolution, agreed with him and extended the mandate until Nov. 30, saying there should be a phased two-month reduction of 300 soldiers, beginning Oct. 1, "taking into account the conditions prevailing at the time."
The U.N. Preventive Deployment Force (UNPREDP) was originally deployed to prevent conflicts elsewhere in the former Yugoslavia from spilling into Macedonia.
It includes nearly 500 U.S. troops, similar-sized contingents from Finland, Denmark, Norway and Sweden, and about 50 soldiers from Indonesia.
"We fully support a message of sustained, undiminished international commitment to UNPREDEP and the region," U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson told the council.

When the Security Council in November 1996 renewed UNPREDEP's mandate until May 31 it also called for a phased 300-man reduction, to be completed by April 30. But on April 9 the council suspended the drawdown because of unrest in Albania.

A 6,350-member U.N.-authorised force under Italian command is deployed in Albania to help protect relief supplies amid chaos that followed the collapse this year of several get-rich-quick "pyramid" schemes in which many Albanians lost their savings.
